judgements.reason: NumberFieldArithmetic already has Layers 1–4 largely in Tau Ceti and still needs the finite-place completion dictionary, the imported local ramification filtration with Hilbert's different formula, Dedekind's cycle-type theorem and rank-one unit certificates. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion still needs power-residue and Hilbert symbols with higher reciprocity through unbuilt global class field theory, Christol and automatic sequences, Hermite/Smith/rational canonical forms, Dobrowolski-type bounds with dynamical heights, and Galois-module theory (Noether, Hilbert–Speiser, Fröhlich).

ClassicalGroups needs one Lie-theoretic tower (Weyl character formula, group-level classification for GL/SL/SO/Sp and O_n, Schur-polynomial characters, branching, GT bases and generators) on top of a large Tau Ceti base of gl_n highest weights, Schur–Weyl duality, Weyl modules, weylDimension and GT counts. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion's missing theory is broader and has deeper imports: CFT-based higher reciprocity, Hilbert–Speiser with Kronecker–Weber, Fröhlich class-group theorems, Christol, Dobrowolski bounds and canonical heights through the unbuilt height machine.

AlgebraicTopology, with only relative singular chains started, must stack subdivision and excision, cellular homology with cofibrations and cellular approximation, Eilenberg–Zilber/Künneth, the Cartan–Leray and Serre spectral sequences, cup/cap products with Poincaré–Lefschetz duality, and relative Hurewicz and Whitehead, and it imports smooth triangulation and an orientation/degree API. ClassicalGroups' remaining Weyl character formula, group-level classification, branching and GT bases sit on a large existing Tau Ceti representation-theory base.

GlobalNumberFields, with places, weak approximation and ray class groups already in Tau Ceti, still needs standard arithmetic layers: error-term lattice counting, adeles and ideles with compactness and strong approximation, the idelic ray dictionary, adele base change, Hecke characters and infinity types, and orders with Picard groups. AlgebraicTopology needs a deeper stack through excision, cellular homology, the Künneth/Cartan–Leray/Serre spectral sequences, Poincaré duality and Hurewicz–Whitehead, plus smooth triangulation.

GlobalNumberFields' missing theory is classical adelic and ideal-theoretic arithmetic on top of built places and ray class groups. K2SymbolsBrauer needs Steinberg groups, Matsumoto's theorem, tame symbols and Bass–Tate/Weil reciprocity, and imports Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory (plus construction, localization, dévissage, spectra) and Tate's theorem K₂(F)/m ≅ H² resting on Poitou–Tate duality and global class field theory.

DerivedDeRhamCohomology needs homotopy-coherent foundations (presentable derived sheaves, coherent Kan extensions, animated rings) and crystalline and log-crystalline cohomology beneath its cotangent-complex, derived de Rham, Cartier and quasisyntomic layers. K2SymbolsBrauer shares the stable ∞-categorical baseline for spectra, but also imports Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory with Quillen's Theorems A/B, plus construction and localization, and continuous Galois cohomology with Poitou–Tate and global class field theory for Tate's theorem, on top of Matsumoto, tame-symbol and Weil-reciprocity theory.

DerivedDeRhamCohomology's missing theory is the derived-algebra and crystalline foundation: ∞-categorical enhancement, cotangent complex, derived de Rham with filtrations and crystalline comparison. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves needs Shimura data and canonical models, Hilbert–Blumenthal and PEL moduli of polarized abelian schemes, Deligne–Pappas integral models, compactifications, Weil I/II étale cohomology and Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, and its recorded closure already contains DDR's derived-completion and ∞-categorical inputs.

LocalGaloisDeformationRings needs Galois deformation functors and Kisin's potentially semistable and Barsotti–Tate rings, built from period rings, admissibility, Breuil–Kisin and Fontaine–Laffaille modules and formal generic fibres. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves needs the whole Shimura-variety, PEL-moduli and compactification theory for abelian schemes, local smooth representation theory, Weil I/II étale cohomology and Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, a much larger stack (recorded closure 165 versus 45 external stages).

LocalGaloisDeformationRings needs local p-adic Hodge theory, Breuil–Kisin modules, formal geometry and deformation algebra. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations needs far more: essentially all of HilbertModularVarieties (Shimura curves, integral models, Čerednik–Drinfeld), Weil I/II, integral modular curves and Jacobians, the geometric p-adic comparison theorems, and Jacquet–Langlands with local Langlands for GL₂ via the trace formula, before building Eichler–Shimura/Deligne representations and local–global compatibility.

AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations' missing theory is the Galois-representation construction and its compatibilities, built on Shimura curves, Weil II and p-adic comparison. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs most of those inputs (its Hsieh branch uses Hilbert Galois representations and CM points, and its recorded closure contains AGR's) and adds BSW overconvergent cohomology of GL₂ over number fields, Deligne–Ribet and Katz CM measures with q-expansion principles and Igusa towers, EHLS unitary p-adic L-functions on PEL Shimura varieties with toroidal compactifications and doubling integrals, and Klingen families on eigenvarieties.

MotivicEtaleKTheory must build higher Chow groups, the Voevodsky–Rost norm-residue theorem, the motivic spectral sequence, étale K-theory with Quillen–Lichtenbaum and regulators, over Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory, Borel's theorem and Poitou–Tate. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs comparably deep machinery several times over (Hilbert and PEL unitary Shimura varieties with toroidal compactifications and Igusa towers, overconvergent cohomology of arithmetic groups, CM measures and q-expansion principles, doubling integrals, eigenvariety families), a clearly broader missing stack even without its modularity-dependent Heegner link (about 300 external stages once its roadmap-level PEL, automorphic-bundle and Hilbert prerequisites are followed, against 144).

Both rest on the same K-theory and motivic core (Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory of rings and schemes, higher Chow groups, the motivic spectral sequence, Borel's regulator theorem, Suslin's K₃ comparison and the Bloch–Wigner regulator), to which Polylogarithms adds only Goncharov's weight-three complexes, Zagier statements and curve regulator complexes. MotivicEtaleKTheory must also build the norm-residue theorem (sheaves with transfers, motivic Steenrod operations, Rost motives), étale K-theory with Quillen–Lichtenbaum and Tate's K₂ theorem, none of which Polylogarithms' checkpoint link to M.8 mathematically requires.

RankZeroOneBSD, with only Mordell–Weil, Néron–Tate heights, 2-descent and the formal L-series in the library, needs modularity of elliptic curves, metaplectic twist nonvanishing, general Gross–Zagier with Waldspurger, Kolyvagin's Heegner-point and Kato's Euler systems, Iwasawa main conjectures and several p-adic L-functions. Polylogarithms' K-theoretic regulator stack (Borel, Suslin, motivic cohomology, Goncharov), though deep, is a much smaller body of missing theory.

RankZeroOneBSD's recorded closure contains 12 of HilbertModularVarieties' 13 stages, because Shimura curves and Hilbert moduli feed modularity, Gross–Zagier and Heegner-point theory. On top of that it needs modularity lifting, general Gross–Zagier and Waldspurger formulas, Kolyvagin and Kato Euler systems, Iwasawa main conjectures, p-adic L-functions and the branch-specific leading-term arguments.

NumberFieldArithmetic, with Layers 1–4 largely in Tau Ceti, still needs the completion dictionary, the local lower-numbering filtration with Hilbert's different formula, Dedekind's theorem and unit certificates, all classical algebraic number theory. K2SymbolsBrauer needs Steinberg groups, Matsumoto's theorem and tame-symbol reciprocity plus imported Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory with plus construction and spectra, and Tate's K₂ theorem via Poitou–Tate duality and global class field theory.

MotivicEtaleKTheory needs a very deep K-theoretic and motivic tower: Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory of rings and schemes, higher Chow groups, the norm-residue theorem, the motivic spectral sequence, étale K-theory with Quillen–Lichtenbaum, Borel regulators, and Tate's theorem with Poitou–Tate. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations needs a comparably deep but broader arithmetic-geometric stack (integral modular and Shimura curves with Jacobians and Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, étale cohomology through Weil I/II, geometric p-adic comparison theorems, local Langlands and Jacquet–Langlands for GL₂ via the trace formula), so its missing theory is somewhat larger (recorded closure 335 versus 144 stages).

ClassicalGroups' remaining Weyl character formula, group-level classification (with SO/Sp/O), Schur-polynomial characters, branching and GT bases and generators build on a large sorry-free Tau Ceti base: gl_n highest weights, Weyl modules, weylDimension, GT pattern counts and Schur–Weyl duality. GlobalNumberFields still has nine largely unbuilt layers: power-saving lattice counting with ray-class main terms, adeles and ideles with compactness and strong approximation, the idelic ray dictionary, topological adele base change (needing NFA's unbuilt semilocal decomposition), Hecke characters and infinity types, and orders with Picard groups.

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion's missing theory is broad but mostly shallow, its deep parts being higher reciprocity through global CFT, Galois-module theorems (Noether, Hilbert–Speiser, Fröhlich), Christol, Dobrowolski-type bounds and dynamical heights. AlgebraicTopology must build one long stacked tower (excision, cellular homology with cofibrations, Künneth/Cartan–Leray/Serre spectral sequences, cup/cap products with Poincaré–Lefschetz duality, relative Hurewicz and Whitehead) and also imports smooth triangulation and an orientation/degree API.

Polylogarithms' needs are the K-theoretic regulator stack: Borel's theorem, Suslin's K₃ comparison, K-theory of schemes, higher Chow groups and the motivic spectral sequence, plus the Bloch and Goncharov constructions. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs Hilbert and PEL unitary Shimura varieties with compactifications and Igusa towers, overconvergent cohomology of arithmetic groups, CM p-adic measures, doubling zeta integrals, eigenvarieties and Galois-representation inputs, a far broader missing stack.

LocalGaloisDeformationRings needs only local p-adic Hodge theory, Breuil–Kisin modules and deformation algebra. RankZeroOneBSD's recorded closure contains most of it (local deformation rings feed modularity lifting for elliptic curves) and adds Gross–Zagier and Waldspurger formulas, Heegner-point and Kato Euler systems, Iwasawa main conjectures and p-adic L-functions.

DerivedDeRhamCohomology's missing theory is a foundational derived-algebra stack: ∞-categorical enhancement and animated rings, cotangent complex, derived completion, derived de Rham with Hodge and conjugate filtrations, crystalline and log-crystalline comparison. AutomorphicPadicLFunctions needs Hecke-character distributions and Iwasawa algebras, overconvergent cohomology of arithmetic groups, Hilbert and PEL unitary Shimura varieties with compactifications and Igusa towers, CM measures, doubling integrals and eigenvarieties, whose p-adic inputs already include DDR's derived-completion layers.

NumberFieldArithmetic, with Layers 1–4 largely in Tau Ceti, still needs the completion dictionary, the imported local lower-numbering filtration with Hilbert's different formula, Dedekind's theorem, subfields and rank-one unit certificates. GlobalNumberFields has only Layers 0–2 built and still needs error-term lattice counting, the whole adelic and idelic development with compactness and strong approximation, adele base change (itself needing NFA's semilocal decomposition), Hecke characters and infinity types, and orders with Picard groups.

K2SymbolsBrauer's missing theory is classical K₂ plus imported Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory, homotopy theory and Tate's theorem with Poitou–Tate duality. HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves needs Shimura data and canonical models, PEL and Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli of polarized abelian schemes, integral models at all p, compactifications and automorphic bundles, local smooth representations, Weil I/II étale cohomology and Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, a much larger stack (recorded closure 165 versus 37 stages).

Polylogarithms needs the K-theoretic regulator stack (Borel's theorem, Suslin's K₃ comparison, Quillen–Waldhausen K-theory of rings and schemes, higher Chow groups, the motivic spectral sequence) plus the Bloch–Wigner and Goncharov constructions. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations needs a clearly larger stack: integral modular and Shimura curves with Čerednik–Drinfeld uniformization, étale cohomology through Weil I/II, geometric p-adic comparison theorems, and local Langlands and Jacquet–Langlands for GL₂ via the trace formula, with Eichler–Shimura and local–global compatibility on top.
